notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the source pages hit a bug in my own script, and the tool then blocked any more calls for this turn. So I haven't read any pages from your approved sites: not Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes, or the Catholic and Orthodox sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for every point, so I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from my own memory, not your sources.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start by reading these pages:
- **Traditional readings, verse by verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ecclesiastes-11/, biblehub.com/commentaries/ecclesiastes/11-1.htm through 11-10.htm (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Matthew Henry), studylight.org, and preceptaustin.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's Notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon sermons on vv. 1, 4 and 6 (spurgeon.org), Ligonier, Desiring God, The Gospel Coalition, and the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org).
- **Other views:** netbible.org translator notes, especially on vv. 1–2 (whether these verses are about generosity or about spreading out investments) and v. 10; bibleodyssey.org; and Catholic and Orthodox material on newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org (such as the Church Fathers on Ecclesiastes).
- **Popular modern teaching:** for example, how "cast your bread upon the waters" is used in prosperity teaching, as the approved sites describe it.

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL after each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
